V1.scale: At the 256 KB probe stack cap, 1000 notifiers (1000 bytes) completed and 2000 (2000 bytes) overflowed, giving a per-frame cost of ~130-230 bytes. Extrapolating linearly to the 1 MB evaluation stack (4x the probe cap, minus ~30 KB base overhead): overflow threshold is approximately 4,400-8,800 notifiers; conservatively about 5,000 notifiers overflow the 1 MB stack. One input byte per notifier (all bytes >= 0x80), so about 5,000 bytes of input. This is the densest encoding: the fuzz test reads one byte per loop iteration.

V2.scale: At the 256 KB probe stack cap, 1000 cancel handlers (1000 bytes) completed and 2000 (2000 bytes) overflowed, giving a per-frame cost of ~130-230 bytes (same as V1). Extrapolating linearly to the 1 MB evaluation stack (4x the probe cap, minus ~30 KB base overhead): overflow threshold is approximately 4,400-8,800 cancel handlers; conservatively about 5,000 cancel handlers overflow the 1 MB stack. One input byte per handler (all bytes >= 0x80), so about 5,000 bytes of input. This is the densest encoding: the fuzz test reads one byte per loop iteration.
